title: Three rolls on one Wednesday, then diesel gave way
paragraphs: This cycle started with an expiry day. On Wednesday 30 September Brent's November contract stopped trading at $106.31 and December, about $7.50 lower, became the front month. NY Harbor diesel and RBOB gasoline rolled from October to November the same day. Every number in this table is on the new contracts, so the drop from EIA's last physical Brent ($113.96 on Tuesday) to the futures is mostly the roll and the normal premium of prompt oil in a backwardated market, not a crash.

On the new contracts the story is diesel. Brent December rose from $98.03 to $102.25 between Wednesday and Friday, while diesel futures slipped from $4.69 to $4.50 a gallon. The diesel crack narrowed from $98.87 to $86.80 a barrel in three sessions. Gasoline barely moved, and the 3-2-1 held in the mid-60s.
Next roll to watch: WTI November expires on Tuesday 20 October. The EIA release on Wednesday 7 October will show whether the physical diesel crack followed the futures lower.
